title: Most haunted places in Australia and the dark history behind them
excerpt: Explore Australia's most haunted places, from Monte Cristo Homestead to Aradale Asylum and Port Arthur: convict history, tragedy and ghost sightings endure.
content:
Australia's most haunted place is widely considered to be Monte Cristo Homestead in Junee, New South Wales — a Victorian mansion soaked in tragedy, unexplained deaths, and over a century of ghost sightings. Yet it is far from alone. From Tasmania's brutal convict settlements to Victoria's crumbling asylums and South Australia's copper-mining ghost towns, the continent holds some of the most deeply unsettling locations in the Southern Hemisphere.

Key takeaways

  • Monte Cristo Homestead in Junee is considered Australia's most haunted private home, associated with multiple deaths and tragedies across its history.
  • Aradale Lunatic Asylum in Ararat, Victoria, is widely considered Australia's most haunted and most extensively documented paranormal site, with 13,000 deaths over 130 years.
  • Picton, a quaint town south-west of Sydney, is reputedly Australia's most haunted town, with paranormal activity reported across multiple sites.
  • Port Arthur carries the weight of two dark chapters: a harsh convict settlement and a 1996 massacre that claimed 35 lives.
  • Fremantle Prison, built by convicts in 1855, saw 44 people executed within its walls before closing as a maximum-security facility.

Australia's most haunted places and their dark histories

Australia's colonial past — built on convict labour, brutal penal conditions, and the forced confinement of the mentally ill — has left a legacy of grief embedded in its oldest buildings. The locations below are drawn from paranormal research, documented ghost tour records, and historical accounts from state archives and national media. They are grouped not by fear factor but by the weight of verified dark history behind them.

Monte Cristo Homestead — Junee, NSW

  • Location: Junee, New South Wales
  • Built: 1884–85
  • Type: Victorian homestead (private residence)
  • Status: Closed to the public since January 2025

Monte Cristo Homestead in Junee is widely regarded as Australia's most haunted house, with a history that's every bit as dark as its reputation. Among its most tragic incidents, a maid reportedly fell or was pushed from an upper balcony to her death.

A caretaker allegedly kept a mentally ill family member chained in the servant's quarters for years. The original owners are said to haunt the home, as well as a caretaker who was murdered there in 1961 and a boy who was kept hidden in the homestead's cottage for many years. The house has been closed to the public since January 2025.

Port Arthur Historic Site — Tasmania

  • Location: Tasman Peninsula, Tasmania
  • Operational: 1830–1877 (penal colony)
  • Type: Former convict settlement and penal colony
  • Key fact: Site of Australia's worst modern mass shooting

Set on the Tasman Peninsula in Tasmania, this former convict settlement operated from 1830 to 1877, housing prisoners in what became one of the most notorious sites in Australia's penal history. This prison used what was called the "silent system," where convicts wore hoods or masks while in each other's company and occasionally spent several days without seeing any lights or hearing any sounds.

More than 1,000 convicts perished within Port Arthur's walls during its 47 years of operation. The nearby Isle of the Dead served as the final resting place for many, and the island allegedly contains 1,646 unmarked convict graves. The tragic events of 1996 added yet more carnage to the site: on 28 April, a gunman opened fire on tourists, killing 35 men, women and children. Ghost stories have been documented at Port Arthur since 1870, long predating the modern massacre. Toptenz.net reported:

"From the disturbing history of the treatment of the prisoners, to the island where over a thousand bodies have been buried, to the deadly massacre of 1996, this site has a deeply dark and horrifying past."

Aradale Lunatic Asylum — Ararat, Victoria

  • Location: Ararat, Victoria (205 km west of Melbourne)
  • Operational: 1865–1993
  • Type: Psychiatric institution (now closed)
  • Key fact: An estimated 13,000 deaths on site

The Aradale Mental Hospital, originally called the Ararat Lunatic Asylum, opened in 1865 and closed in 1993, housing up to 1,000 patients across 70 buildings at one time. Both electroshock therapy and lobotomy were performed on a mass scale at Aradale.

Around 13,000 people died there, mostly due to the horrific psychiatric treatments carried out over 130 years. The notorious J Ward, completed in 1887, housed the most violent patients and criminals not fit for prison. Three men were hanged here and buried in unmarked graves, placed upright and facing the asylum — reputedly to ensure their spirits would remain confined within its walls forever. Today, ghost tours explore exclusive parts of Australia's largest abandoned lunatic asylum.

Old Melbourne Gaol — Melbourne, Victoria

  • Location: Russell Street, Melbourne, Victoria
  • Operational: 1845–1924
  • Type: Prison (now a museum)
  • Key fact: 133 people executed, including Ned Kelly

The Old Melbourne Gaol was first constructed starting in 1839, and during its operation between 1845 and 1924 it held and executed some of Australia's most notorious criminals, including bushranger Ned Kelly and serial killer Frederick Bailey Deeming.

The gaol saw 133 executions in total. Notable among them was Ned Kelly — one of Australia's most infamous bushrangers — and Deeming, who was suspected by some to be Jack the Ripper. The ghost of Elizabeth Scott, the first woman executed at the prison, is believed to still haunt the gaol, and paranormal sightings, strange voices, and a monstrous ghostly figure have been recorded hovering in doorways. Visitors on the Old Melbourne Gaol night tour are warned to watch cell 17 closely — it's said to be one of the most haunted cells in Australia.

Fremantle Prison — Fremantle, Western Australia

  • Location: Fremantle, Western Australia
  • Operational: 1855–1991
  • Type: Maximum-security prison (now a World Heritage Site)
  • Key fact: Built by convicts; 44 people executed

As the first building on Western Australia's World Heritage Site list, Fremantle Prison first opened in 1855, built by the convicts themselves — and from there, tragic tales of whipping and death by gallows ensued, with 44 people ultimately executed within its walls.

The facility ceased operation in 1991 and is now a public museum managed by the Western Australian government. Paranormal activity, strange sensations, and weird noises have been reported by visitors. It was a place of incarceration for locally-sentenced prisoners, many of whom were executed for murder and other crimes. The Fremantle Prison torchlight tour on Wednesday and Friday nights is one of Perth's most popular after-dark experiences, and cameras have been known to malfunction near the gallows.

Q Station (North Head Quarantine Station) — Sydney, NSW

  • Location: North Head, Manly, New South Wales
  • Operational: 1832–1984
  • Type: Quarantine station (now a heritage hotel)
  • Key fact: Over 500 deaths from infectious disease

The Q Station operated as a quarantine station from 1832 to 1984 and is widely considered one of Australia's most haunted locations. It was built on the harbour to prevent the spread of infectious diseases such as typhus, cholera, and smallpox from incoming ship passengers — and many of those confined within its walls perished.

At least 50 ghosts are said to reside at the property, arising from the 600 deaths that occurred at the station before its 1984 closure. The eeriest zones include the morgue and the former hospital ward, where guests on the Q Station ghost tour have reported objects moving on their own.

Old Adelaide Gaol — Adelaide, South Australia

  • Location: Gaol Road, Adelaide, South Australia
  • Operational: 1841–1988
  • Type: Prison (now a museum)
  • Key fact: 45 people executed over 147 years

In operation from 1841 to 1988, the Old Adelaide Gaol was the first permanent gaol of South Australia. Over those 147 years, 44 men and one woman were hanged within its walls.

A young girl has been sighted walking and dissolving through the wall of the guard tower, while a man has been seen strolling along the upper walkway. Visitors have reported feeling overwhelming sadness in the rooms used by executioners, and unexplained lights and noises are a recurring feature of the haunting. The Adelaide Gaol ghost tours run regularly and are among the most popular in South Australia.

Kapunda — South Australia

  • Location: Kapunda, South Australia (1 hour north of Adelaide)
  • Type: Historic copper-mining town
  • Key fact: Widely called Australia's most haunted town

Nestled in South Australia's Barossa wine region, the old copper-mining hub of Kapunda is said by many to be Australia's most haunted town. Kapunda was a busy mining town in the early 1800s, and the North Kapunda Hotel opened in 1849 to service the region.

Ghosts believed to inhabit the North Kapunda Hotel include Sarah, adopted by a brothel madame after her mother was murdered; Hue, a miner who died in room 14 following an amputation; and Kapunda's first Mayor, Dr Henry Smyth-Blood, believed to have returned to the hotel after his death. St John's Cemetery in Kapunda is also reportedly haunted by an unwed mother searching for her baby, who was forcibly taken from her.

Picton — New South Wales

  • Location: Wollondilly Shire, 80 km south-west of Sydney, NSW
  • Type: Historic colonial town
  • Key fact: Dozens of paranormal sites concentrated in one small town

Picton is the most haunted town in Australia — and it's not a self-proclaimed title. A ghost story sticks out in almost every corner of the town. Picton's disused Redbank Range Tunnel extends 180 metres and was the site of multiple suicides when it served as a railway between 1867 and 1919.

Brent Hilbrink-Watson and his sister Jasmine Flaxman run Wollondilly Tours, a spooky look at Picton after dark. The town is rich in convict murders, bushranger activity, construction accidents, and is even where Australia's first serial killing is said to have taken place. The graveyard, maternity hospital, and town hall are all said to be haunted in Picton, so you can make a day — or night — of your paranormal intrigue.

Beechworth Lunatic Asylum — Beechworth, Victoria

  • Location: Beechworth, north-east Victoria
  • Operational: 1867–1995
  • Type: Psychiatric institution (now a heritage venue)
  • Key fact: More than 9,000 patients died during its 128 years of operation

Beechworth Lunatic Asylum in north-east Victoria offers the most personalised paranormal tradition in Australia — the ghost of Rosina, who tends the garden, is the most specifically characterised apparition at any Australian haunted location, and the overnight investigation programme is among the country's most serious.

Beechworth Lunatic Asylum in Beechworth, Victoria, is reportedly haunted by several ghosts of departed patients. The Beechworth Asylum ghost tours attract visitors from across Australia drawn to its combination of genuine psychiatric history and intense reported paranormal activity. The asylum's chilling records of deaths, locked wards, and brutal treatments make it one of the most historically significant dark-tourism sites in the country.

FAQs

What is Australia's most haunted place?

Aradale Lunatic Asylum in Ararat, Victoria, is widely considered Australia's most haunted and most extensively documented paranormal site, with 13,000 deaths over 130 years, the ghost of Rosina in the garden, and intense investigation reports from J Ward. Monte Cristo Homestead in Junee is also frequently cited as the top contender, particularly for Australia's most haunted private building.

What is the most haunted house in Australia?

Monte Cristo Homestead in Junee is often called Australia's most haunted house, known for stories of tragic accidents, a "hidden" child, and a protective presence. The homestead was built in 1884–85 and has been associated with multiple violent and suspicious deaths stretching across more than a century.

What is the most haunted town in Australia?

While many places claim a spooky past, Kapunda in South Australia has a notorious reputation. Known as the most haunted town in Australia, it was once a booming and violent copper mining town, and its most infamous location is the North Kapunda Hotel. Picton, NSW, is a close rival, with haunted sites spread across the entire township.

Is Port Arthur really haunted?

With well over a thousand people dying at Port Arthur, many believe those souls have never left the location. Unexplained events and ghost stories have been documented there since 1870, long predating the modern era of paranormal tourism. The site also carries the grief of the 1996 massacre, adding a modern layer to its centuries-old darkness.

Can you visit these haunted places in Australia?

Most of these sites are open to the public and offer dedicated ghost tours. At Port Arthur, visitors can join a 90-minute lantern-lit ghost tour of the ruins. Old Melbourne Gaol, Fremantle Prison, Aradale, the Q Station, and the Old Adelaide Gaol all run regular night tours. Monte Cristo Homestead, however, has been closed to visitors since early 2025.
